questions.prompt: Which integer represents 7 metres below sea level?
questions.explanation: Positions below sea level are represented by negative integers, so 7 metres below sea level is -7.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify integers in different real life situations.

questions.prompt: A learner starts at -3 on a number line and moves 8 steps to the right. Where does the learner land?
questions.explanation: Moving right means adding. -3 + 8 = 5.
questions.learningOutcome: Represent integers on a number line in different situations.

questions.prompt: Work out -12 + 7.
questions.explanation: Adding 7 to -12 moves 7 steps towards zero, giving -5.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out addition of integers in different situations.

questions.prompt: Work out 6 - (-9).
questions.explanation: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive value: 6 - (-9) = 6 + 9 = 15.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out subtraction of integers in different situations.

questions.prompt: The temperature in Limuru changed from -2 degrees C to 5 degrees C. What was the increase?
questions.explanation: The change is 5 - (-2), which is 7 degrees C.
questions.learningOutcome: Use integers to solve real life problems.

questions.prompt: Which value is equal to -4 + (-6)?
questions.explanation: Adding two negative integers keeps the sign negative and adds their sizes: 4 + 6 = 10.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out operations involving integers.

questions.prompt: Work out 2/3 + 1/4.
questions.explanation: The common denominator is 12. 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so the sum is 11/12.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out combined operations on fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Work out 5/6 - 1/3.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out operations on fractions in real life situations.

questions.prompt: A class planted vegetables on 3/4 of a 28 metre plot. How many metres of the plot were planted?
questions.explanation: Three quarters of 28 is 28 x 3/4 = 21.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fractions to solve real life problems.

questions.explanation: First add inside the brackets: 1/2 + 3/4 = 5/4. Then 5/4 - 1/4 = 4/4 = 1.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the correct order of operations in fractions.

questions.prompt: Work out 3/5 divided by 9/10.
questions.explanation: Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal: 3/5 x 10/9 = 30/45 = 2/3.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out operations on fractions in real life situations.

questions.prompt: A farm harvested 2 1/2 sacks of beans on Monday and 1 3/4 sacks on Tuesday. How many sacks were harvested in total?
questions.learningOutcome: Apply operations on fractions to real life situations.

questions.prompt: Convert 3/8 into a decimal.
questions.explanation: Dividing 3 by 8 gives 0.375.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert fractions to decimals in different situations.

questions.prompt: Which fraction is equal to the recurring decimal 0.666...?
questions.explanation: The recurring decimal 0.666... is the decimal form of 2/3.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert recurring decimals into fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Round 45.678 to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The third decimal digit is 8, so the hundredths digit rounds up from 7 to 8.
questions.learningOutcome: Round off a decimal number to a required number of decimal places.

questions.prompt: Write 0.00456 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 3 places to the right to get 4.56, so the power of 10 is -3.
questions.learningOutcome: Express numbers in standard form in different situations.

questions.prompt: Work out 3.4 + 2.15 x 2.
questions.explanation: Multiplication is done first: 2.15 x 2 = 4.30. Then 3.4 + 4.30 = 7.70.
questions.learningOutcome: Carry out combined operations on decimals in the correct order.

questions.prompt: Express 7280 to two significant figures.
questions.explanation: The first two significant figures are 7 and 2. The next digit is 8, so 72 rounds to 73 hundreds.
questions.learningOutcome: Express numbers to a required significant figure in real life situations.

questions.prompt: What is 17 squared?
questions.explanation: 17 squared means 17 x 17, which is 289.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the squares of numbers from tables in different situations.

questions.prompt: What is the square root of 196?
questions.explanation: The square root of 196 is 14 because 14 x 14 = 196.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the square roots of numbers from tables in different situations.

questions.prompt: A square garden has an area of 225 square metres. What is the length of one side?
questions.explanation: The side of a square is the square root of its area. The square root of 225 is 15.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply square roots in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Work out 2 squared plus 5 squared.
questions.explanation: 2 squared is 4 and 5 squared is 25. Their sum is 29.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out squares of numbers in different situations.

questions.prompt: Work out the square root of 625 plus 8 squared.
questions.explanation: The square root of 625 is 25 and 8 squared is 64. 25 + 64 = 89.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out squares and square roots of numbers in different situations.

questions.prompt: A bus travels 180 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time: 180 km divided by 3 hours is 60 km/h.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out rates in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Simplify the ratio 12:18.
questions.explanation: Divide both parts by their highest common factor, 6. The ratio becomes 2:3.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out ratios in different situations.

questions.prompt: KSh 480 is shared in the ratio 5:7. How much does the first person receive?
questions.explanation: The total number of parts is 12. Each part is KSh 480 divided by 12, which is KSh 40, so 5 parts is KSh 200.
questions.learningOutcome: Divide quantities in given ratios in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Increase KSh 800 by 15 percent.
questions.explanation: 15 percent of 800 is 120. Adding the increase gives 800 + 120 = 920.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out percentage increase of quantities in real life situations.

questions.prompt: A bicycle priced at KSh 2500 is reduced by 12 percent. What is the new price?
questions.explanation: 12 percent of 2500 is 300. The reduced price is 2500 - 300 = 2200.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out percentage decrease of quantities in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Which situation shows direct proportion?
options: Cost and number of identical notebooks bought
Number of workers and time taken for the same job
Age of a learner and shoe size every month
Temperature and number of pupils in class
questions.correctAnswer: Cost and number of identical notebooks bought
questions.explanation: If the price per notebook is fixed, buying more notebooks increases the total cost in the same ratio.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify direct proportions in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Six workers can complete a task in 8 days. If the same task is shared equally by 12 workers, how many days should it take?
questions.explanation: Doubling the number of workers halves the time for the same amount of work, so 8 days becomes 4 days.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out indirect proportions in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Express the fraction 3/8 as a ratio.
questions.explanation: A fraction a/b can be written as the ratio a:b, so 3/8 is 3:8.
questions.learningOutcome: Express fractions as ratios in real life situations.

questions.prompt: If 4 kg of flour makes 60 chapatis, how many chapatis can 10 kg of flour make at the same rate?
questions.explanation: One kilogram makes 60 divided by 4, which is 15 chapatis. Ten kilograms make 10 x 15 = 150 chapatis.
questions.learningOutcome: Use proportions to solve real life problems.

questions.prompt: Factorize 6x + 9.
questions.explanation: The common factor of 6x and 9 is 3, so 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
questions.learningOutcome: Factorize algebraic expressions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Factorize x^2 + 5x.
questions.explanation: Both terms contain x, so take x as the common factor: x^2 + 5x = x(x + 5).
questions.learningOutcome: Factorize algebraic expressions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Simplify 6a^2 divided by 3a.
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients and subtract powers of a: 6a^2 divided by 3a = 2a.
questions.learningOutcome: Simplify algebraic fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Evaluate 3x - 2y when x = 4 and y = 5.
questions.explanation: Substitute the values: 3(4) - 2(5) = 12 - 10 = 2.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate algebraic expressions by substituting numerical values.

questions.prompt: Simplify 7p + 3q - 2p + q.
questions.explanation: Combine like terms: 7p - 2p = 5p and 3q + q = 4q.
questions.learningOutcome: Simplify algebraic expressions by grouping like terms.

questions.prompt: Simplify (x + 2x)/3.
questions.explanation: The numerator is x + 2x = 3x. Dividing 3x by 3 gives x.
questions.learningOutcome: Simplify algebraic fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Factorize 4m - 12n.
questions.explanation: The common factor is 4. Dividing the terms by 4 gives m and 3n.
questions.learningOutcome: Factorize algebraic expressions in different situations.

questions.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 11 and x - y = 3.
questions.explanation: Adding the two equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7. Then y = 4.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve linear equations in two unknowns by elimination method.

questions.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 13 and x - y = 2.
questions.explanation: From x - y = 2, y = x - 2. Substitute in 2x + y = 13 to get 3x - 2 = 13, so x = 5 and y = 3.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve linear equations in two unknowns by substitution method.

questions.prompt: When 3x + 2y = 16 and x - 2y = 4 are added, which equation is obtained?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates y because 2y and -2y add to 0. The result is 4x = 20.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve linear equations in two unknowns by elimination method.

questions.prompt: Two pens and one ruler cost KSh 65. One pen and one ruler cost KSh 40. What is the cost of one pen?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the second cost from the first removes the ruler and leaves the cost of one pen: 65 - 40 = 25.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply linear equations in two unknowns in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Solve 4a + 2b = 22 and a + b = 8.
questions.explanation: From a + b = 8, b = 8 - a. Substitution gives 4a + 2(8 - a) = 22, so a = 3 and b = 5.
questions.learningOutcome: Solve linear equations in two unknowns by substitution method.

questions.prompt: Three mangoes and two oranges cost KSh 110. If a mango costs x shillings and an orange costs y shillings, which equation represents this statement?
questions.explanation: Three mangoes cost 3x and two oranges cost 2y, so the total cost is 3x + 2y.
questions.learningOutcome: Form linear equations in two unknowns in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Which pair of equations is satisfied by x = 2 and y = 5?
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 2 and y = 5 gives 2 + 5 = 7 and 3(2) - 5 = 1.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize solutions of linear equations in two unknowns.

questions.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle with radius 7 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2 x pi x radius. 2 x 22/7 x 7 = 44 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the circumference of a circle in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 14 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Circumference is pi x diameter. 22/7 x 14 = 44 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the circumference of a circle in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Find the length of a 90 degree arc in a circle of radius 14 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: A 90 degree arc is one quarter of the circumference. The circumference is 88 cm, so the arc is 22 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the length of an arc of a circle in different situations.

questions.prompt: Find the perimeter of a 60 degree sector of radius 21 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: The arc length is 60/360 of 132 cm, which is 22 cm. The perimeter is 21 + 21 + 22 = 64 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the perimeter of a sector of a circle in different situations.

questions.prompt: A circular track has circumference 88 m. Find its radius using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Using C = 2 x pi x r, 88 = 2 x 22/7 x r. This gives r = 14 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Use circle measurements to solve real life problems.

questions.prompt: A semicircular flower bed has radius 10 m. Find its perimeter using pi = 3.14.
questions.explanation: The perimeter of a semicircle is half the circumference plus the diameter: 31.4 + 20 = 51.4 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the perimeter of a sector of a circle in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Find the area of a circle with radius 7 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Area is pi x r x r. 22/7 x 7 x 7 = 154 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the area of a circle in different situations.

questions.prompt: Find the area of a 90 degree sector of radius 14 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: A 90 degree sector is one quarter of the circle. The circle area is 616 cm2, so the sector area is 154 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the area of a sector of a circle in different situations.

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a cube with side 5 cm.
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 equal square faces. Its surface area is 6 x 5 x 5 = 150 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the surface area of cubes in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a cuboid measuring 6 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm.
questions.explanation: Surface area is 2(lw + lh + wh). 2(24 + 18 + 12) = 108 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the surface area of cuboids in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Find the total surface area of a closed cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm using pi = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Total surface area is 2 x pi x r x (r + h). 2 x 22/7 x 7 x 17 = 748 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the surface area of cylinders in real life situations.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism is 10 cm long. Its triangular end is a right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its total surface area.
questions.explanation: The rectangular faces total 10(3 + 4 + 5) = 120 cm2. The two triangular ends total 2 x 1/2 x 3 x 4 = 12 cm2, so the total is 132 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the surface area of a triangular prism in different situations.

questions.prompt: An irregular shape covers 34 full squares and 8 half squares on a square grid. What is its estimated area?
questions.explanation: Eight half squares make 4 full squares. 34 + 4 = 38 square units.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out the area of irregular shapes using square grids.

questions.prompt: Find the simple interest on KSh 8000 at 10 percent per annum for 2 years.
questions.explanation: Simple interest is PRT/100. 8000 x 10 x 2 / 100 = 1600.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate simple interest in real life situations.

questions.prompt: KSh 8000 earns simple interest at 10 percent per annum for 2 years. What is the total amount?
questions.explanation: The interest is KSh 1600. The amount is principal plus interest: 8000 + 1600 = 9600.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate simple interest and amount in real life situations.

questions.prompt: KSh 10000 is invested at 5 percent compound interest per annum for 2 years. What interest is earned?
questions.explanation: The amount after 2 years is 10000 x 1.05 x 1.05 = 11025. The interest is 11025 - 10000 = 1025.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate compound interest per annum step by step up to three years.

questions.prompt: A machine worth KSh 50000 depreciates by 10 percent per year. What is its value after 2 years?
questions.explanation: After one year the value is 50000 x 0.9 = 45000. After the second year it is 45000 x 0.9 = 40500.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out depreciation per annum step by step up to three years.

questions.prompt: A radio is bought on hire purchase with a deposit of KSh 6000 and 12 monthly instalments of KSh 1200. What is the hire purchase price?
questions.explanation: The instalments total 12 x 1200 = 14400. Add the deposit: 14400 + 6000 = 20400.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out hire purchase in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Which tools are most suitable for constructing a perpendicular bisector accurately?
options: A ruler and a pair of compasses
questions.correctAnswer: A ruler and a pair of compasses
questions.explanation: A perpendicular bisector is accurately constructed using equal arcs from a pair of compasses and a straight line from a ruler.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct perpendicular lines in different situations.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
questions.explanation: The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is (n - 2) x 180 degrees. For 5 sides, this is 3 x 180 = 540 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify angle properties of polygons in different situations.

questions.prompt: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon has interior angle sum 720 degrees. Dividing by 6 gives 120 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify angle properties of regular polygons up to a hexagon.

questions.prompt: What is each exterior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: Exterior angles of any polygon add to 360 degrees. For a regular pentagon, 360 divided by 5 is 72 degrees.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify angle properties of polygons in different situations.

questions.prompt: What is the name of a circle that passes through all three vertices of a triangle?
questions.explanation: A circumcircle is constructed to pass through all the vertices of a triangle.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct circles passing through the vertices of a triangle.

questions.prompt: What is the name of a circle that touches all three sides of a triangle?
questions.explanation: An incircle lies inside a triangle and touches each of its three sides.
questions.learningOutcome: Construct circles touching the sides of a triangle.

questions.prompt: A 12 cm line is divided in the ratio 1:2. What are the two lengths?
questions.explanation: The total number of parts is 3. Each part is 12 divided by 3, which is 4 cm, so the lengths are 4 cm and 8 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Divide a line proportionally in different situations.

questions.prompt: Which ordered pair represents x = -3 and y = 4?
questions.explanation: Coordinates are written as (horizontal value, vertical value), so x = -3 and y = 4 is (-3, 4).
questions.learningOutcome: Identify points on the Cartesian plane in different situations.

questions.prompt: In which quadrant is the point (-5, -2)?
questions.explanation: A point with a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate lies in the third quadrant.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify points on the Cartesian plane in different situations.

questions.prompt: For the equation y = 2x + 1, what is y when x = 3?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 3: y = 2(3) + 1 = 7.
questions.learningOutcome: Generate values in a table for a linear equation.

questions.prompt: For y = 3x - 2, what are the y-values when x = -1, 0 and 1?
questions.explanation: Substitute each x-value: 3(-1) - 2 = -5, 3(0) - 2 = -2, and 3(1) - 2 = 1.
questions.learningOutcome: Generate a table of values for a linear equation.

questions.prompt: What is the point of intersection of the lines x + y = 6 and x - y = 2?
questions.explanation: Solving the equations gives x = 4 and y = 2, so the lines meet at (4, 2).
questions.learningOutcome: Solve simultaneous linear equations graphically in different situations.

questions.prompt: What type of line is represented by y = 4 on a Cartesian plane?
options: A diagonal line through the origin
questions.explanation: All points on y = 4 have the same y-coordinate, so the graph is a horizontal line.
questions.learningOutcome: Draw linear graphs from equations on a Cartesian plane.

questions.prompt: A graph scale says 1 cm represents 5 learners. How many centimetres should represent 25 learners?
questions.explanation: Divide 25 learners by 5 learners per centimetre to get 5 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine an appropriate scale for a linear graph.

questions.prompt: On a map, 1 cm represents 2 km. What actual distance is represented by 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Each centimetre represents 2 km, so 6 cm represents 6 x 2 = 12 km.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert scale length to actual length in real life situations.

questions.prompt: An actual distance of 500 m is represented by 5 cm on a drawing. What is the scale ratio?
questions.explanation: Convert 500 m to 50000 cm. The ratio 5:50000 simplifies to 1:10000.
questions.learningOutcome: Write linear scales in ratio form in different situations.

questions.prompt: A map has a scale of 1:50000. What actual distance is represented by 3 cm on the map?
questions.explanation: 3 cm represents 150000 cm. This is 1500 m, which is 1.5 km.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret linear scales in ratio form in different situations.

questions.prompt: Convert the statement scale 1 cm represents 4 m into ratio form.
questions.explanation: Convert 4 m to 400 cm. The scale is therefore 1 cm to 400 cm, or 1:400.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert linear scale from statement form to ratio form.

questions.prompt: A classroom is 8 m long. Using the scale 1 cm represents 2 m, what length should be drawn?
questions.explanation: Divide the actual length by 2 m per centimetre: 8 divided by 2 = 4 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert actual length to scale length in real life situations.

questions.prompt: A road is 18 km long. On a map, 1 cm represents 3 km. What map length represents the road?
questions.explanation: Divide 18 km by 3 km per centimetre to get 6 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Represent length to a given scale in different situations.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is drawn 6 cm by 4 cm using the scale 1 cm represents 5 m. What are the actual dimensions?
questions.explanation: Multiply each drawing length by 5 m. 6 cm represents 30 m and 4 cm represents 20 m.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply scale drawing in real life situations.

questions.prompt: Which solid has two circular faces and one curved surface?
questions.explanation: A cylinder has two equal circular faces joined by one curved surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common solids from the environment.

questions.prompt: How many equal square faces are in the net of a cube?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 equal square faces, so its net contains 6 squares.
questions.learningOutcome: Sketch nets of cubes in different situations.

questions.prompt: A cuboid measures 8 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. What is its surface area?
questions.explanation: Surface area is 2(lw + lh + wh). 2(40 + 32 + 20) = 184 cm2.
questions.learningOutcome: Work out surface area of solids from nets in different situations.

questions.prompt: On the top face of a cuboid, the sides are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the shortest distance between opposite corners on that face?
questions.explanation: The diagonal of the rectangular face forms a right triangle. 6 squared plus 8 squared is 100, so the distance is 10 cm.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the distance between two points on the surface of a solid.

questions.prompt: Which shapes make up the net of a cone?
questions.explanation: A cone opens into a circular base and a sector that forms the curved surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Sketch nets of cones in different situations.

questions.prompt: Find the mean of 6, 8, 10 and 12.
questions.explanation: Add the values to get 36, then divide by 4 values. The mean is 9.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the mean of a set of discrete data.

questions.prompt: Find the median of 5, 9, 4, 7 and 12.
questions.explanation: Arrange the data as 4, 5, 7, 9, 12. The middle value is 7.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the median of a set of discrete data.

questions.prompt: Find the mode of 3, 4, 4, 6, 7, 7, 7 and 8.
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. The number 7 appears three times.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the mode of a set of discrete data.

questions.prompt: A bar graph uses a scale of 1 unit for 5 learners. How many learners are shown by a bar 7 units high?
questions.explanation: Each unit represents 5 learners, so 7 units represent 7 x 5 = 35 learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret bar graphs of data from real life situations.

questions.prompt: A line graph shows 12 seedlings on Monday and 18 seedlings on Tuesday. What was the increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 18 - 12 = 6 seedlings.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret line graphs of data from real life situations.

questions.prompt: A table records maize harvests as January 18 bags, February 25 bags and March 22 bags. Which month had the highest harvest?
questions.explanation: February has 25 bags, which is greater than 18 bags and 22 bags.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret data from real life situations.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of getting a head when tossing a fair coin once?
questions.explanation: A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes, head and tail, so the probability of a head is 1/2.
questions.learningOutcome: Express probability outcomes in fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of rolling an even number on a fair six-sided die?
questions.explanation: The even outcomes are 2, 4 and 6. That is 3 favourable outcomes out of 6, which simplifies to 1/2.
questions.learningOutcome: Express probability outcomes in fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: A bag has 3 red balls, 2 blue balls and 5 green balls. What is the probability of picking a blue ball at random?
questions.explanation: There are 10 balls altogether and 2 are blue. The probability is 2/10, which simplifies to 1/5.
questions.learningOutcome: Express probability outcomes in fractions in different situations.

questions.prompt: In 40 throws of a die, the number 6 appeared 12 times. What is the experimental probability of getting a 6?
questions.explanation: Experimental probability is successful outcomes divided by total trials: 12/40 = 3/10.
questions.learningOutcome: Write experimental probability outcomes in different situations.
